newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet to fight Koniambo expropriation.
newsitem.headline: Eramet to fight Koniambo expropriation.

text.p: Nickel producer Eramet said in a statement it had received a letter from the Ministry of Industry on Friday in which the government announced it had decided to start a procedure of expropriation of mining rights for the Koniambo field held by Eramet's Societe Le Nickel.
The company said it would use all legal means in its possession to prevent such a decision, which would cause it "considerable prejudice" and would affect its financial outlook, being taken.
The Koniambo field is in New Caledonia.
Eramet said the Ministry gave no reasons for the procedure in the letter.

The company said it believed that under the current laws and regulations in New Caledonia such a decision could not be justified. SLN had been operating the mine for more than a century and intended to increase production, Eramet said.

On January 30, the French government and officials of the two main political parties of the French South Pacific island of New Caledonia agreed to reallocate mining reserves within the territory so that local Kanak independence groups could go ahead with plans to build a nickel plant in the north.
Part of the proposal was to swap mining rights between Koniambo and the Poum field so that Koniambo could supply the ore to the Kanak nickel plant.
Eramet is 55.5 percent owned by the French state.
France hopes an agreement on greater autonomy for the territory could head off a referendum on self-determination which is set for 1998.
